clue.text: Home of Kronenbourg beer hosting heads of Stella Artois and Carlsberg

the opening letter of the lager brand

explanation.surface: A beer-lover's note on where Kronenbourg comes from, mentioning two rival lager brands.
explanation.walkthrough: Kronenbourg is brewed near Strasbourg, so the definition is a plain geographical fact rather than a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is the French region around Strasbourg where the Kronenbourg brewery has long been based.

clue.text: Notice spiritual class felt void, lacking guidance

parts.note: an ad is a notice, short for advertisement
RI is religious instruction, a school lesson

indicators.note: something void has been emptied, so the word loses its insides and only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone notices a spiritual class felt empty and aimless.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the old name for a British school subject now usually called RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift floats without steering, so the word describes anything aimless or without direction.

clue.text: Second mass park function uplifted active parent

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A park event, briefly mentioned, lifts the spirits of a busy parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces are joined and then the whole string is turned upside down. A 'rec' is British slang for a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer mom is the American stereotype of a busy suburban mother ferrying children to sports, an energetic parent.

clue.text: Artist's hat replaced by autumn time in country house

indicators.note: one item is swapped out and another put in its place, so a fragment of the house word is exchanged

parts.note: taken as written; this is what is taken out
October, abbreviated, is a month of autumn
a chateau is a French country house

explanation.surface: An artist's hat is swapped for something seasonal at a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HAT out of CHATEAU and put OCT in its place. The 's here is 'is', joining artist to the wordplay.

clue.text: Clothing company, as it were, still reported

parts.note: stillness or quiet is peace

explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' flags that company only means TWO via the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece is a garment in two parts, such as a suit or bikini, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Maestro and wife face losing piano

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

p is the musical marking for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A conductor and his wife face life without their piano.
explanation.walkthrough: PHIZ, an old word for face (from physiognomy), loses its P and follows W.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiz is an expert, someone brilliant at something, as a maestro is.

clue.text: After sixteen pints, is alcoholic's belly ready for food?

parts.note: a peck is two gallons, sixteen pints
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker sixteen pints in wonders whether a big belly can still find room for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A peck is an old dry measure of two gallons, which makes sixteen pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is the informal British word for feeling slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Roofless hub in Florida key

parts.note: the American spelling of centre, a hub

explanation.walkthrough: 'In Florida' asks for the American spelling CENTER, which then loses its C. 'Key' wants to be a Florida island; it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is the keyboard key pressed to confirm a command or start a new line.

clue.text: Less refined English craft here rendered by Jürgen

explanation.surface: A German translator renders an English craft piece into something cruder.
explanation.walkthrough: Jürgen stands for any German speaker, so 'here' must be translated into German.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down-to-earth, so earthier means cruder or less refined.

clue.text: Ornate centrepiece in iron company replicated

indicators.note: the centrepiece is what stands in the middle, so only the two central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the metal word
Co is the abbreviation for company
the company abbreviation repeated

explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the eighteenth-century style known for elaborate, highly decorated ornament.

clue.text: Angler knocked back roll and cold drink

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A fisherman downs a bread roll and a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTA, C and SIP are joined, then the whole reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Piscator is a literary word for a fisherman, from the Latin for fish.

clue.text: Some peek at Simon's towering bloomer

only some of the words is needed, a run of letters spanning them

parts.note: the run from the end of peek to the start of Simon

explanation.surface: A glimpse of Simon's prize bloom, shooting up high.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EKATSIM run across 'peek at Simon's'; read upwards they give MISTAKE. 'Bloomer' looks like a flower; it is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a blunder in British slang, an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Maniacal, largely European guards kept fit regularly

indicators.note: guards surround what they protect, so the nationality word encloses the other letters

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A frantic European bodyguard keeps fit by training regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' reads as a noun, people protecting someone, but it is a verb meaning surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means wildly agitated and frantic, close to a crazed or manic state.

clue.text: Lewis's partner westbound discovers old address

parts.note: Lewis and Harris is a single island in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: Lewis's companion, travelling west, comes across an old home address.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris are two parts of one Scottish island, so Harris is Lewis's partner. 'Address' looks like a place to live; it is a form of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirrah is an archaic form of address used to a man or boy of lower status.

clue.text: Journalist on Times entertaining without underlying theme

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor on a newspaper

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, here twice
ex means without, as in ex dividend

explanation.surface: A reporter at The Times hosting a party has no unifying theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but gives two Ts, which hold EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtext is the meaning that lies beneath the surface of a text or conversation, an implied theme.

clue.text: Rock figureheads at this place launch career again

parts.note: to mount a campaign is to launch it
to career is to rush headlong
once more, again

explanation.surface: Heads of rock bands relaunch their careers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock figureheads' sounds like rock-band leaders, but means presidential heads carved in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota has the heads of four US presidents carved into its granite cliff.

clue.text: Sidekick possibly writing song that's suitable

parts.note: an oppo is a mate or opposite number, a sidekick for example
one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
a tune is a song

explanation.surface: A sidekick might be writing a song that fits the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is informal British for a colleague or partner. Writing is R because it is one of the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed and fitting the circumstances, so convenient or appropriate.

clue.text: Film with Ford Galaxy perhaps handling brutal climbing

indicators.note: to handle something is to hold it, so the celebrities word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a galaxy of celebrities is a group of stars

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing goes upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: brutal in the sense of raw, crude

explanation.surface: A Ford Galaxy, a people carrier, being driven roughly up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford Galaxy' reads as the car; the definition stops at Ford, meaning Harrison Ford, and Galaxy starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is the 1977 film in which Harrison Ford played Han Solo.

clue.text: Dressing likewise around coaster, vessel buoyant

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the likewise word encloses the coaster word

a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
buoyant spirits are up

explanation.surface: A sailor's yarn about dressing up, a coastal trader and a boat that floats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' and 'vessel' both suggest shipping, but the coaster here is a drinks mat; only vessel is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato ketchup is a sauce, and dressing can mean a sauce or condiment added to food.

clue.text: Tradesman's first question with local: status of windows here?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the trade word

parts.note: the opening letter
to ask is to question
the local is your nearby pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A glazier asks at the pub how the windows are coming along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like glass panes for the tradesman; it means program windows on a computer. A local is British for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The taskbar on a computer screen shows which program windows are open and active.

clue.text: Bony thing emptied earlier into decomposed matter

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its middle, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something bony, hollowed out long ago, buried in rotting soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, so it is quite literally a bone.

clue.text: Universal greeting about peace, as hippie appears?

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so the greeting word wraps the peace word

parts.note: a nod is a silent greeting
sh is a call for quiet, peace

explanation.surface: A hippie turns up with a universal salute about peace.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal audiences. The definition is a description: hippies were famously barefoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippies were stereotypically barefoot, and unshod means not wearing shoes.

clue.text: Modify Tesla, among others, in spring

indicators.note: in places one thing inside the other, so the car word sits within the spring word

a Tesla is one of many electric vehicles, EVs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' could be the inventor or the magnetic unit; here it is the car maker, an example of an electric vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise something is to amend or alter it, which is to modify it.

clue.text: See you collecting university prize

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A goodbye as someone picks up a university award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like a noun but is the verb, to prize something.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to hold it dear, which is to value it highly.

clue.text: Deafening silence perhaps after studio finally axes Flash Gordon, Blessed being dismissed separately

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, and separately means the letters go one at a time from different spots
finally points to the closing letter only of the studio word

parts.note: the closing letter
the x and y axes of a graph
a flash or moment is a mo
taken as written
God is the blessed being; these letters leave the name one by one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed being' is GOD, whose G, O and D are removed separately from GORDON to leave RON. Brian Blessed starred in the film Flash Gordon.

clue.text: Material Girl

explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a heavy cotton twill fabric used for jeans, and it is also a common woman's name.

clue.text: Swinish behaviour here possibly finished when first husband gone

clue.text: Succeeded in French?
